title: Distractor Misconception Matrix

calculation_error.description: Wrong formula, wrong arithmetic, wrong input substitution
calculation_error.quality_assessment: Strong — calculation errors map directly to common CMA traps (variance sign confusion, denominator choice, allocation base errors)

formula_confusion.description: Confuses one formula with another (e.g., NPV vs IRR, FIFO vs LIFO COGS)
formula_confusion.quality_assessment: Strong — well-documented exam trap in DEFECT_LIBRARY.md (DL-001 pattern)

terminology_confusion.description: Confuses similar accounting terms (e.g., 'cost' vs 'expense', 'liability' vs 'equity')
terminology_confusion.quality_assessment: Acceptable — common but some distractors are surface-level word swaps

framework_confusion.description: Applies wrong framework (e.g., US GAAP when IFRS applies, absorption when variable costing needed)
framework_confusion.quality_assessment: Strong — framework errors are high-discrimination distractors

classification_error.description: Classifies item incorrectly (e.g., operating vs financing cash flow, current vs non-current)
classification_error.quality_assessment: Strong — classification errors are authentic CMA exam traps

policy_misunderstanding.description: Misunderstands accounting policy choice (e.g., LIFO liquidation, revenue recognition timing)
policy_misunderstanding.quality_assessment: Acceptable — less well-targeted; some policy distractors are straw-man arguments

scope_error.description: Applies Part 2 concepts in Part 1 context or vice versa
scope_error.quality_assessment: Weak — most scope-error distractors are obviously wrong; only advanced candidates would be tempted

misconception_coverage_gaps.gap: No distractors targeting 'unit-of-account confusion' (e.g., capitalizing costs that should be expensed at a different unit)
Underrepresentation of 'materiality vs precision' distractors (quantitative thresholds for investigation)
No distractors targeting 'data governance ethical dilemmas' (confidentiality vs transparency tradeoffs)

case_bank_misconception_coverage: Cannot be assessed — 97.8% of case items have empty ExplanationWrong fields. Misconception mapping for case distractors requires full EW authoring first.
finding: 992 absolutist-language instances detected. However, per DISTRACTOR_REWRITE_CANDIDATES_S90.md, 99% of these are legitimate usage ('only' in technical contexts like 'recognize revenue only when...'). Only 10-12 instances represent genuine absolutist-distractor problems.
